concepts.title: Erosion of Power of Indian Rulers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Erosion of Power of Indian Rulers' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic process by which local Indian monarchs were stripped of executive sovereignty, revenue rights, and military forces through coercive colonial treaties.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Erosion of Power of Indian Rulers'.
questions.a: Measures like the Subsidiary Alliance and refusal to honor adopted heirs undermined native royal authority.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Erosion of Power of Indian Rulers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Nawabs lose their power (source: hess205.txt lines 15-50)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Grievances of Peasants and Sepoys' refers to.
questions.a: The cumulative economic hardship endured by agrarian communities combined with religious and operational dissatisfaction among native soldiers in colonial army service.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Grievances of Peasants and Sepoys'.
questions.a: Exorbitant agrarian taxation and army regulations overriding religious taboos created deep dissatisfaction.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Grievances of Peasants and Sepoys' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The peasants and the sepoys (source: hess205.txt lines 51-80)

concepts.title: British Social Reforms and Native Reaction

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'British Social Reforms and Native Reaction' refers to.
questions.a: Legislative initiatives and educational interventions introduced by colonial authorities that traditional sections of Indian society interpreted as threats to their faith and social structure.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'British Social Reforms and Native Reaction'.
questions.a: State-sponsored social legislation and patronage of Christian missions created fears of cultural erosion.

questions.q: Under which section is 'British Social Reforms and Native Reaction' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Responses to reforms (source: hess205.txt lines 81-110)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Contemporary Accounts and Rumours of 1857' refers to.
questions.a: Personal memoirs and community reports capturing popular mistrust, secret communications, and widespread rumours regarding greased cartridges preceding the rebellion.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Contemporary Accounts and Rumours of 1857'.
questions.a: Memoirs like Majha Pravaas and From Sepoy to Subedar reflect deep-seated suspicions of British intentions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Contemporary Accounts and Rumours of 1857' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Through the Eyes of the People (source: hess205.txt lines 111-180)

concepts.title: Outbreak of Revolt: From Meerut to Delhi

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Outbreak of Revolt: From Meerut to Delhi' refers to.
questions.a: The transformation of localized military resistance into a coordinated nationwide movement following the capture of Delhi and endorsement by the Mughal sovereign.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Outbreak of Revolt: From Meerut to Delhi'.
questions.a: Military mutinies in Barrackpore and Meerut rapidly expanded into a broader struggle under Bahadur Shah Zafar.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Outbreak of Revolt: From Meerut to Delhi' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: A Mutiny Becomes a Popular Uprising & From Meerut to Delhi (source: hess205.txt lines 181-240)

concepts.title: Regional Leadership and Centres of Rebellion

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Regional Leadership and Centres of Rebellion' refers to.
questions.a: The multi-regional expansion of resistance led by local princes, deposed noblewomen, zamindars, and military captains across northern and central India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Regional Leadership and Centres of Rebellion'.
questions.a: Prominent regional leaders mobilized forces locally while acknowledging the overarching nominal authority of the Mughal Emperor.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Regional Leadership and Centres of Rebellion' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The uprising spreads (source: hess205.txt lines 241-290)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'British Military Counter-Offensive and Suppression' refers to.
questions.a: The multi-year military campaign launched by the East India Company using imperial reinforcements, siege tactics, and political clemency to quash the rebellion.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'British Military Counter-Offensive and Suppression'.
questions.a: The Company deployed heavy military force, suppressed key regional hubs, and offered land guarantees to break resistance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'British Military Counter-Offensive and Suppression' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Company Fights Back (source: hess205.txt lines 291-340)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Post-1857 Administrative and Policy Reorganization' refers to.
questions.a: The constitutional and administrative restructuring enacted by the British Empire under the Act of 1858 to establish direct Crown control over India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Post-1857 Administrative and Policy Reorganization'.
questions.a: The British Crown assumed direct governance, reorganized army composition, and reversed territorial expansion policies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Post-1857 Administrative and Policy Reorganization' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Aftermath (source: hess205.txt lines 341-400)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Khurda Uprising of 1817' refers to.
questions.a: An early 19th-century rebellion of Paik militia and peasants in Odisha led by Buxi Jagabandhu against severe British fiscal and salt policies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Khurda Uprising of 1817'.
questions.a: The Paik Rebellion of 1817 demonstrated early popular resistance caused by heavy land revenue demands and currency disruption.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Khurda Uprising of 1817' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Khurda Uprising – A Case Study (source: hess205.txt lines 401-490)

concepts.title: Calculation of Historical Time Intervals and Elapsed Years

questions.q: Calculate the number of years between the Khurda Uprising in start_year and the Great Revolt in end_year.. Use the method 'Calculation of Historical Time Intervals and Elapsed Years'. Work with: end_year = 150, start_year = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of elapsed_years.
questions.a: 50 years

questions.q: How many years elapsed between the imposition of the Subsidiary Alliance on Awadh in start_year and its final takeover in end_year? Use the method 'Calculation of Historical Time Intervals and Elapsed Years'. Work with: end_year = 100, start_year = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of elapsed_years.
questions.a: 75 years

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Calculation of Historical Time Intervals and Elapsed Years' refers to.
questions.a: Calculating the exact interval in years between major historical events, administrative enactments, or revolts during colonial rule.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Calculation of Historical Time Intervals and Elapsed Years'.
questions.a: The time elapsed between two historical milestones is calculated by finding the difference between the ending year and starting year.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Calculation of Historical Time Intervals and Elapsed Years', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: elapsed_years = end_year - start_year
